pr_body:
This pr fixes (all?) the (re)parenting issues that NavigationAgent Nodes have.

Calling NavigationAgent setup with a get_parent() function only once in _ready() was troubesome. What if agent is moved or removed from tree and rejoins? what if parent is switched, what if agent is created with scripts, ... and so many options to mess NavigationAgents parents up.

Fixes #54812

Supersedes #54904 which was stale and used another ready notification to fix some of this but calling _ready() twice is too dangerous with user scripts.

issue_context.title: Reparenting a NavigationAgent2D into a SubViewport causes navigation to fail
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.dev.20211108.official [596865366]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

On project run I reparent a container Node2D containing a TileMap and an Enemy with a NavigationAgent2D child into a SubViewport. This causes the NavigationAgent2D to fail at finding a parent.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3820082/140990387-5d88acba-977e-4bce-ac86-a01895b498ce.mp4

This can be fixed in these ways:

a) Have the container Node2D parented to the SubViewport in the scene beforehand (you can not edit the SubViewport's children in the editor this way.)

b) Create a NavigationAgent2D on the Enemy after it's been moved into the SubViewport.

My expectation is that the NavigationAgent2D's world would be updated upon reparenting so that navigation still works. I also don't see a way to update the agent's world in GDScript.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the attached MRP in a recent Godot 4.0 pre-alpha build and run the default scene. To disable the reparent, select the Node of the default scene and toggle the exported Reparent bool, then run the scene again.

### Minimal reproduction project

[nav-reparent-mrp.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/7507380/nav-reparent-mrp.zip)

review_comments: I dont remember the details but there was a specific issue where a user managed to corrupt the agent connection with the wrong parent due to shuffling node parents with subscenes and this fixed it. Thats also why I left such a large comment so I wouldn't remove it myself in a few months because I would also assume it wouldn't ever be triggered.
